title: Go: Type Switch
description: Use type switches to handle multiple concrete types through an interface value in Go.

steps.title: Basic type switch on interface{}
steps.description: Write a function `describe(v interface{})` that uses a type switch to print the kind and value. Handle `int`, `string`, `bool`, and `default`. Print using `fmt.Printf("%s: %v\n", kind, v)`.
hints: Type switch syntax: switch v := x.(type)

verification.failureMessage: Print the type kind and value for each case.

steps.title: Custom interface with type switch
steps.description: Define an interface `Shape` with `Area() float64`. Create `Circle` and `Rectangle` structs implementing it. Write `printShape(s Shape)` that type-switches and prints shape-specific fields. Use `fmt.Printf("Circle(r=%.1f): Area=%.1f\n", c.Radius, c.Area())`.
hints: Type switch works on any interface type
Access concrete fields inside each case
Fallthrough is implicit in type switches

verification.failureMessage: Print circle radius and rectangle dimensions with area.

steps.title: Type switch with error handling
steps.description: Write `process(v interface{}) (string, error)` that type-switches and returns an error for unsupported types. Use `fmt.Errorf` for error creation. Call with `int`, `string`, `[]byte`, and `chan int`. Print results using `fmt.Printf("Result: %s, Err: %v\n", result, err)`.
hints: Return errors for types your function can't handle
Type switch can return from each case

verification.successMessage: Type switch with error handling works!
verification.failureMessage: Print both the result and any error for each input.

steps.title: Nested type switches and type assertion
steps.description: Write a `flatten(v interface{})` function that recursively handles `[]interface{}` slices. Use a type switch to detect slices, then recursively flatten. Print flattened elements using `fmt.Printf("Element %d: %v\n", i, elem)`.
hints: Recursive call inside the slice case
Track depth to avoid infinite recursion

verification.successMessage: Nested type switch with recursion works!
verification.failureMessage: Print each flattened element with its index.
